questions.q: How does the summary suggest you use your ego?
a: As a tool to upgrade your behavior and confidence
As a reason to ignore other people's advice
As proof that you are better than others
As a shield against ever taking a risk
questions.why: The first lesson says you can use your ego to boost yourself through posture, body language and a confident tone.

questions.q: Why is the past not a reliable guide to the future?
a: Past events need not repeat, and our memories are subjective
The future changes faster than the past ever did
People forget most of what happened to them
History always follows predictable cycles
questions.why: The second lesson says we assume patterns predict what comes next, though our memory is subjective and the brain favors safety.

questions.q: What happens when you break a big project into micro-steps?
a: You become more willing to start and more likely to finish
The project ends up taking much longer overall
You lose sight of the final goal
You need fewer deadlines to stay motivated
questions.why: The summary says our readiness to start small, achievable projects is much greater than when facing a huge objective.

questions.q: What is confirmation bias, as the summary describes it?
a: Seeking information that supports what you already believe
Judging people mainly by their physical appearance
Drawing broad conclusions from very little evidence
Assuming the worst about strangers you meet
questions.why: The third lesson defines confirmation bias as looking for and interpreting information to confirm your current beliefs.

questions.q: What should you do when you have an assumption about someone?
a: Ask them for clarification and look beyond appearance
Keep the assumption private and watch them closely
Avoid them until you find hard proof
Test the assumption with other people first
questions.why: The third lesson advises asking the person for clarification and remaining open rather than judgmental.
